acceptance.output_evidence: (1) WHICH ROUND-1 S3 KEYS ALREADY CARRY A NAME-SHAPED COMPONENT, AND WHAT REMOVING THEM WOULD REQUIRE. MEASURED over the live plane, not reasoned: every object in opal-data-ycharts listed and every segment of every key run through the constructor's OWN new ladder (_check_segment), so the census asks exactly the question the fix asks and cannot drift from it. 38 keys, 251 segments, 6 segments refused -- ALL of them NOT_A_DECLARED_SHAPE and ZERO refused as DISPLAY_NAME_SHAPED or EMAIL_SHAPED. THE ANSWER AS ASKED IS: NONE. The six are worth naming anyway, because 'refused by the new ladder' and 'carries a name' are different sets. All six are the same segment, 'irpt-variants-20260911-comparison', in six sibling keys under research/20260911/variants/synthetic-firm/synthetic-advisor/requests/. It is 33 characters and SEGMENT_WORD_RE admits 32 -- a LENGTH OVERFLOW on a structural word, not a name -- and those keys sit under research/, which is not a declared prefix family at all: they were written by the CRO's variants worker, not by s3_evidence_key. Of the 38 keys, 5 are under firms/ (the declared families this constructor builds) and 33 under research/; ALL FIVE DECLARED-FAMILY KEYS PASS THE NEW LADDER CLEANLY. WHAT REMOVING THEM WOULD REQUIRE: nothing, on this evidence -- there is nothing name-shaped to remove. If the question is what removing a name-shaped key WOULD require, the answer is an S3 copy-then-delete under a new key plus a rewrite of every reference to the old one, and the references are the hard part: an AnalysisReport row's vendor_artifact and release.protected_pdf_ref both carry a storage_key, the irpt-jobs table carries attempt keys, and a receipt is content-addressed by a key it names. S3 has no rename. That is why the face's bound makes the refusal FORWARD-ONLY, and on this evidence the bound costs nothing: the forward-only fix is also a complete one. (2) DID THE CLOSED REASON ENUM LOSE A DIAGNOSTIC AN OPERATOR NEEDS? NO -- because the diagnostic MOVED rather than being deleted, and arm (d) measures the move in BOTH directions: 0 occurrences of the injected value in the response, and 18 of 18 correlation ids resolving to an internal record that DOES carry it. A redaction that destroys the diagnostic is switched off by the first person debugging at 2am, and then the leak returns permanently with a good reason attached. THREE THINGS AN OPERATOR GENUINELY LOST, stated rather than argued away: (i) THE ONE-GLANCE CAUSE. A failure that showed 'BadZipFile: File is not a zip file' now shows INVALID_INPUT plus corr-<12 hex>, and the cause needs a second lookup. That is a real cost in minutes and it is the price of the property. (ii) RESOLUTION WITHOUT LOG ACCESS. The correlation id is only useful to someone who can read the function's log group. A support person who can see a response but not CloudWatch has strictly less than before. Whether that population exists is a product question I cannot answer from here and am flagging rather than assuming. (iii) THE RESIDUAL CLASS IS UNOBSERVED. 14 reasons cover the outcomes the six families reach, and UNEXPECTED is a MEMBER rather than an escape hatch, so an unclassified failure still gets a code a consumer can branch on. The defence against it quietly becoming the common case is that reason_for() maps by TYPE, so a new exception class lands in UNEXPECTED visibly. But NOBODY COUNTS how often it is returned. A standing count of reason codes by frequency would catch the drift -- and that is a monitor, which bound 2 forbids this project outright. The tension is real: the moratorium is correct AND it means this enum's health is unobserved. That is the CVO's to weigh, not mine to resolve. (3) WHICH ERROR PATH COULD I NOT REACH WITH AN INJECTED EXCEPTION. Four, in three kinds, and the first kind is the sharpest. NOT REACHABLE BECAUSE THE CODE IS DEPLOYED NOWHERE: intake/parse.py and intake/corrections.py are in NO function's packaged file list in lambda-source-map.json. Three of the error paths this order fixed live in them -- including the jsonschema ValidationError path, which was the worst of the original ten because a ValidationError's first line quotes the INSTANCE, so a holdings row carrying a client name went into a contract-validation report. They are fixed in the repo, exercised by the local suite, and serve nothing today. An injected exception reaches them in-process and can never reach them in a deployed function, because there is no deployed function containing them. NOT REACHABLE BECAUSE THE PATH IS DEAD ON IMPORT -- and this one CHANGED in this execution: export/download.py's error paths were unreachable in the deployed function because its module-level `import enforce` failed (row W3-S14). That is now CLOSED: enforce.py, errors.py and resolve.py are in the build input, the import closure reads 6 of 6 in the real layout, and the deployed function answers a capabilities invoke at statusCode 200. So this category is empty at the end of this order where it had one member at the start. NOT REACHABLE BECAUSE THE DEPENDENCY WILL NOT FAIL ON DEMAND: the paths that catch an ImportError for pypdf (export/render.py, three of them) and for jsonschema (export/bundle.py). I can force them by manipulating sys.modules, which is a self-wrapping harness and bound 12 forbids it as evidence; in the deployed function they fire only when the layer genuinely lacks the dependency. Their fix is the trivial one -- render the exception's TYPE, not the exception -- and they are asserted by reading rather than by execution. AND ONE CATEGORY THE QUESTION DOES NOT ASK ABOUT BUT THAT BOUNDS THE ANSWER: arm (c)'s census reads EXCEPT HANDLERS, so a public reason built on an ORDINARY RETURN is outside its denominator entirely. One such path existed -- directory/handler.py returned 'ERROR: unsupported op ' + repr(op), reflecting caller input -- and it surfaced only because a directory test failed against a neighbouring change. '0 of 57 except handlers render the exception' is true and is NOT the same claim as 'no public reason carries caller data'. Row IRPT_BCKEND-W3-S15, carried to L10 by name and deliberately not widened here.

Neither module is in any function's file list, so three of the error paths this order fixed serve nothing today. Adding them to a zip would be inventing a deployment this order was not asked to make. Stated in the RT4-AC2 record rather than left to be discovered.

declared_exclusions.reason: Bounds 1 and 2. The only live reads are AWS control-plane, S3, and one read-only Lambda invoke against Opal's own account.

surprises: IRPT_BCKEND-W3-S19: a two-part change was split by the drain -- enforce.py gained a module-level `import errors` whose CODE half merged and whose PACKAGING half did not, so the source map at the tip declared builds for two functions that cannot import. That failure passes CodeSha256, the post-apply plan and the ledger, because all three measure bytes and none measures importability. The same split left the registration disagreeing with the world on five of six functions (triple equality 0 of 6). Repaired for the six functions this order touches; the general shape is not.

IRPT_BCKEND-W3-S20: a sibling is writing to the shared export Terraform state while this order is non-terminal. This order's apply was clean and both readings are in the ledger; half an hour later the same root planned 0 to add, 2 to change, 1 to destroy, and converging it would destroy a live IAM grant, delete 21 command lines of render-host preflight and revert the portal origin. The discriminator is that this order changed no Terraform configuration at all. The amendment sequenced IB-rt-8 behind this order to prevent exactly this, which suggests the sequencing is per-ORDER while the contention is per-ROOT.

IRPT_BCKEND-W3-S21: the irpt-common layer's BUILD_MANIFEST disagrees with the layer that is published -- 637,134 bytes and 159 members recorded against 644,526 and 161 live, with S3 and Lambda agreeing with each other and not with the record. The content is correct, which is why nothing noticed; the record is what a later cell would rebuild from, on a surface three functions share. Reading the published zip rather than the manifest is also what showed enforce.py, errors.py and resolve.py are absent from the layer and must ride the export zip.

IRPT_BCKEND-W3-S22: two modules named dispatch.py collide on the flat sys.path every export module shares, so `import dispatch` resolves to _authz/dispatch.py and IB-rt-8's own tests cannot see export/dispatch.py -- four failures at the pristine tip, before any change of this order's. The deployed case is worse: in a Lambda every packaged module sits flat at /var/task, so a zip carrying both would have one overwrite the other. Latent today and not this order's to rename.
